definitions.explanation: Irregular, unpredictable movements in the atmosphere that cause sudden jolting and shaking of aircraft during flight.

examples.japanese: {飛行機|ひこうき}が{乱気流|らんきりゅう}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: The airplane was caught in turbulence.

examples.japanese: {乱気流|らんきりゅう}のため、シートベルトを{締|し}めてください。
examples.english: Please fasten your seatbelts due to turbulence.

examples.japanese: {激|はげ}しい{乱気流|らんきりゅう}で{機内|きない}の{乗客|じょうきゃく}がけがをした。
examples.english: Passengers inside the plane were injured by severe turbulence.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in aviation contexts. Compound of {乱|らん} (chaotic), {気|き} (air), and {流|りゅう} (flow). Also used metaphorically to describe chaotic or turbulent situations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乱気流|らんきりゅう}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる (to be caught in turbulence)
- {激|はげ}しい{乱気流|らんきりゅう} (severe turbulence)
- {乱気流|らんきりゅう}が{発生|はっせい}する (turbulence occurs)
- {乱気流|らんきりゅう}に{遭|あ}う (to encounter turbulence)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- タービュランス: turbulence (loanword) — used in technical/aviation English contexts
- {気流|きりゅう}: air current — the neutral base term without the "chaotic" element
